lead: there are eleven hours a week when nobody can get you, and not one person in twenty years has asked what happens in them, because a person that open is assumed to have nothing to be unreachable about.
sun: everything else is available. the time, the answer, the house, the version of the story with the bad part left in — out where anyone can reach it, and asking is not a thing that occurs to people about you. the whole of it sits at the surface. what people have met of you is one blank in a schedule, and they file it under the same ease as the rest.
moon: those hours hold one thing. it is small and it is load-bearing, and the whole shelter over it stands on a single upright, with no partial failure available — either it holds or an afternoon takes the roof off. this road runs twenty-eight stations and it has spent all of them separating your two lights, so nothing carries between them. the room gets the spread and nothing else.
pull: eleven hours a week are the only part of you nobody has been inside, and the size the room reads off you is standing on what happens in them.
tension: everyone who knows you would describe you as having nothing covered, and every item they could check backs them up. so a sentence about the eleven hours would have to build its own occasion, and at your size an occasion built for one sentence is an announcement. nothing of yours comes out small. so it goes unsaid by nobody's decision, and when the upright moves, the people nearest you will hear at the same hour as everybody else.
cost: people arrive already inside — no warm-up, no waiting period, no month of proving they are the sort who gets told things. the one stretch that stayed covered has therefore had no practice: you have no procedure for letting a person in, because the rest of you never required one, and the upright has been holding on its own since it went up.

lead: outdoors your size is one item among many. indoors there is nothing to dilute it, and the people who live with you have spent years inside a volume you cannot enter as a guest.
sun: a room has a ceiling, and whatever is in it stays in it. so a middling mood of yours, the kind other people take upstairs and sleep off, arrives at everybody's plate at full width. you have not raised your voice in years and it makes no difference, because the width was never in the voice. the household reads the weather off you before the kettle is on, and adjusts without mentioning it.
moon: you are the one who put the walls up. the routine that holds, the hour things happen at, the arrangement that has meant nobody here wondered where they were sleeping — all of it structural, none of it discussed, and nobody inside it has thought of it as made. the walls are what keep the weather in, and that did not occur to you while they were going up.
pull: you built these walls, and the same walls are what stop your size from going anywhere. nobody who lives here has ever stood in a room of yours without you in it.
tension: the complaint, when it comes, arrives from a twenty-four-year-old describing a childhood, and the person described is warm. that is the difficulty. no incident is in it, no shouting, nothing withheld, no year anyone would call hard. what is in it is a house where one person was always the largest thing present, and a kid who worked out early that a room is quieter when the person who built it is not in it.
cost: money comes in, people get fed, and the arrangements hold through the years that take other houses apart, none of it needing to be announced because none of it has failed. what nobody who grew up in it has is the experience of an ordinary-sized room. the first place each of them moved to on leaving was small and plain and theirs, and no one could have said why.

lead: they fell in behind you the way water finds a slope, each of them certain they were chosen, and you have been walking at your ordinary pace since before the first one arrived.
sun: no offer was made. what draws them is a size, read at a distance as an institution with a programme in it — somewhere to be attached to, with a name and a duration. so people arrange their next four years around you on evidence you did not submit, and by the time you notice, two of them have turned down other things, and one has moved cities for a place that does not exist.
moon: the actual instinct is to walk somebody out. you know the road, you go the whole length with them, and at the edge of the thing they wanted you stop — the work finishes there, cleanly, with nothing further in you for it. what you are performing is a delivery. what they took themselves to have joined was something permanent, and neither of you said either sentence out loud.
pull: you take them the whole way and stop at the line, and they turn round expecting a building, because a person your size was never read as an escort.
tension: afterwards, the ones who left describe being dropped, and the account is accurate up to the last day, which is what makes it hard to answer. the ending was in the arrangement from the beginning and was never stated, because at the beginning nobody asked and it did not occur to you that it needed saying. so the word stands, from four people, over twenty years, and each of them got further with you than they would have anywhere else.
cost: eighteen months with you does what a decade of ordinary supervision cannot, because they turn up already convinced and you know every bend in the road. then the delivery is made. the day after is the one thing you have no instinct for, and by then they have built a life around a person they understood to be staying. you were walking the whole time. neither of you lied.

lead: a man you were at school with described you to a stranger for a minute and a half, and every word of it would have been true when you were eleven. the account has not needed changing since.
sun: what a room settles about you in eight seconds is what a schoolyard settled when you were a child, and the two agree, and the agreement proves nothing except that the same thing is being looked at. so you have gone into new places and skipped the part where a person is unknown — the seat in the middle, the question put to you, the thing somebody tells you at the sink in week one.
moon: one continuous line runs the entire length of it, with no interval anywhere, no stretch where the reading lapsed and had to be picked up again. and it pulls from both ends. people forty years out are still holding theirs taut, and so are you, and neither end has gone slack long enough for anyone to learn what the other would do.
pull: there is no year anybody has to be told about. the record runs unbroken from nine years old to this morning, and a fresh start is the one thing it cannot contain.
tension: changing is not available as an event. other people announce a new city, a stopped habit, a different life, and the announcement works because there is a period before it and a period after. anything you alter gets absorbed into a length that already runs forty years, so the alteration reads as a mood — the same person, going through something. the year you took your whole life apart and rebuilt it was received, politely, as a phase.
cost: nothing about you has to be re-established. you walk into a place that has not met you and are forty years in, with no probation, no proving period, none of the decade others spend assembling it. and nowhere to go and be small. every road out ends in a room that has you sized by friday, and the rest that comes of being unknown is not on offer.
